_README: Human-verified facts that no script could extract, merged into the cards by build_cards.py.
Every entry MUST carry a source URL and the date it was checked.
This file is the only place a human may add a fact by hand. Nothing here may be an opinion.

acute_limit.unit: mg per kg of body weight, per single drink
means: This is not a daily average. It is a limit for ONE serving.
EFSA found that a single slush ice drink of 250 ml (children) or 500 ml (others)
would exceed this limit for every age group.
Reported effects in young children after high intake include nausea, vomiting,
headache, low blood sugar and loss of consciousness.
As of this check there is still no legally binding maximum for glycerol in EU
slush drinks. The UK advises that children under 7 should not drink them.

422.why_this_matters_here: Glycerol appears in 45 of the Indian products in this dataset, and slush ice drinks are widely sold to children in India.

eu_authorisation.note: Banned in food in the EU since 2022. EFSA concluded in May 2021 that titanium dioxide can no longer be considered safe as a food additive, because a concern over genotoxicity could not be ruled out and no acceptable daily intake could be set.

171.why_this_matters_here: India and the United States still permit titanium dioxide. This is the clearest case in the dataset of regulators reaching different conclusions, and the reason is on the record rather than left to guesswork.
